Section: section_1 — The Analogy: The Guessing Game

Lecture lines:
Neural networks start as simple guessing machines.
They classify inputs into random, wrong categories.
A robot guesses cat versus dog pixels.

Planned animations:
Display 'Guessing Game' title in white (#FFFFFF) text.
Fade in two representative guessers, one red (#FF0000), one blue (#0000FF).
Show a target value in yellow (#FFFF00) above guessers.

Section: section_2 — Prerequisite: The Error Surface

Lecture lines:
We visualize error as a mountainous landscape.
Low valleys represent the ideal minimum error.
A ball rolls downhill, seeking the lowest point.

Planned animations:
Display 'Error Surface' title in white (#FFFFFF).
Animate a bowl-shaped landscape representing loss values in light blue (#ADD8E6).
Place a marker in red (#FF0000) representing current loss position.

Section: section_3 — The Core Concept: Backpropagation (The Blame Game)

Lecture lines:
Backpropagation is the game of assigning blame.
We trace error backward, layer by layer.
Each neuron receives feedback on its contribution.

Planned animations:
Display 'The Blame Game' title in white (#FFFFFF).
Animate flow of error backwards from output to input.
Use arrows in green (#00FF00) for visual flow direction.
Highlight connections between layers in gold (#FFD700).
Flash the final weight update node in orange (#FFA500).

Section: section_4 — The Math: Chain Rule in Motion

Lecture lines:
The chain rule connects small weight changes.
It acts as a precise mathematical multiplier.
Tiny changes ripple through connected network gears.

Planned animations:
Display 'Chain Rule' title in white (#FFFFFF).
Show function composition visually as connected pipes in light gray (#D3D3D3).
Visualize derivative flow as movement speed along pipes.
Highlight each pipe segment sequentially in cyan (#00FFFF).
Combine flow rates into a single final vector.

Section: section_5 — Synthesis & Summary

Lecture lines:
Forward pass guesses, calculating initial error.
Backward pass adjusts weights, reducing error.
Repetition makes the network progressively smarter.

Planned animations:
Display 'Summary' title in white (#FFFFFF).
Fade in three key summary bullets in white (#FFFFFF).
Highlight the cycle of predict-error-update in bright green (#00FF00).
